newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris metro blast is ninth bomb attack in France.
newsitem.headline: Paris metro blast is ninth bomb attack in France.

text.p: An explosion in a Paris Metro underground train which killed two people on Tuesday recalled a wave of bombings in which eight died last year blamed on Algerian guerrillas fighting to overthrow their government.

The gas-canister bomb used in the latest bombing at Paris Port Royal metro station recalled last year's bombs -- packed with nails and bolts, a bloody technique used by the fundamentalist Armed Islamic Group (GIA) guerrillas in Algeria.
Following is a chronology of the attacks:

JULY 25 - Gas-canister bomb explodes in rush-hour regional express train at crowded Saint-Michel metro station in central Paris, killing seven. One of the 86 injured died later. Bloodiest attack in France since wave of Middle East-related bombings in mid-1980s.
AUGUST 17 - Gas-canister bomb packed with nails explodes in rubbish bin outside metro station near Arc de Triomphe in heart of Paris, wounding 17 including 11 tourists.
AUGUST 26 - A 25-kg (55-lb) bomb planted alongside high-speed rail line north of central city of Lyon fails to go off because of faulty trigger mechanism.
SEPTEMBER 3 - Pressure-cooker bomb packed with nails and bolts misfires in central Paris open-air market near Place de la Bastille, wounding four. Detonator failed to ignite rest of the explosive.
SEPTEMBER 4 - Police defuse 25-kg (55-lb) gas-canister bomb set to explode in public toilet at crowded open-air central Paris market the day before.
SEPTEMBER 7 - Car bomb explosion injures 14 outside Jewish school in Lyon suburb of Villeurbanne, minutes before students leave for day. School clock running late avoids heavier toll.
SEPTEMBER 27 - Police launch hunt for Khaled Kelkal, Algerian-born petty criminal whose fingerprints were found on August 26 rail-line bomb.

SEPTEMBER 29 - Paramilitary gendarmes kill Kelkal near Lyon, triggering four nights of riots in Vaulx-en-Velin, depressed Lyon suburb where he lived. Row breaks out over whether he could have been captured alive.
OCTOBER 6 - Gas-canister bomb packed with nails and bolts explodes in bin in southeast Paris just hours after Kelkal's funeral, wounding 13.
OCTOBER 7 - Statement in name of GIA claims responsibility for attacks and threatens more. Group says it asked Chirac in August to become a Moslem but he refused.
OCTOBER 17 - Bomb explodes on Paris underground train near Saint-Michel station, wounding 26.
NOVEMBER 2 - Police say they foiled planned car-bombing of a crowded marketplace in northern town of Lille and detained a suspected guerrilla leader in Paris.
JANUARY 22 - Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre says 344 people have been arrested in connection with the bombings and 95 people are still in detention.
DECEMBER 3 - Gas-canister bomb explodes on underground train at central Port Royal station, near Louvre museum, killing two and wounding 47.
